title: Design a gated VCF 9.1 workload-domain convergence
prompt:
Produce the executable architecture for adding the workload domain described in `fixtures/estate-inventory.json` to the existing VCF fleet. The management domain is already at its intended level and must remain unchanged. The workload estate is mixed-version: an apparently natural component-by-component upgrade order crosses an unsupported combination, so the migration must route through a supported VCF-managed path.

Before implementing, use your network research tools to consult current, real Broadcom-published compatibility, interoperability, upgrade-path, and VCF 9.1 upgrade-sequence material. Do not rely only on the checked-in snapshot for that research. Record the source title, reachable URL, consultation date, and the specific conclusion you used in `research.md`; note any disagreement between live material and the pinned snapshot. The live research informs your design, but `fixtures/compatibility-snapshot.json` is the deterministic authority for the artifact and acceptance checks.

Implement the design as a Go package in `architecture/` and a runnable `cmd/vcf-architecture` command. The command must read the inventory and pinned snapshot and write `out/architecture.json`; it must not fetch the network. Add your own table-driven Go tests. The complete package must pass `go test -race ./...`.

`out/architecture.json` is the architecture, not a prose report. Its top level must be an `SddcSpec` that validates against `components.schemas.SddcSpec` in the checked-in `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json`, pinned from tag `9.1.0.0` of the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository. It must also satisfy `schemas/architecture-output.schema.json`. Populate its installer fields from the fixture, model the existing vCenter and NSX as existing deployments, preserve every management-domain component at its current version, and include an ordered `migrationPlan`.

The migration plan must name every workload component from the inventory, state each current and final target version, and attach only gate IDs present in the pinned snapshot. Each ordered step must name its action and all component transitions it performs. The sequence must be executable from the fixture's starting state: every transition must be supported by the snapshot, every required gate and predecessor action must be present, no intermediate state may match a forbidden combination, and every workload component must finish at its inventory target. Do not add migration steps for management-domain components.

The checked-in verifier, schemas, specification, inventory, compatibility snapshot, and `architecture/contract_test.go` are protected acceptance material. Run `python3 -B verifier/verify.py` for the full check. The verifier intentionally does not read or grade `research.md`; research is demonstrated by genuine network use and the record you leave, while acceptance remains deterministic.
